title: Archimedes Screw Pump

introduction.definition: An Archimedes screw pump is a large, slowly rotating screw set at an incline in an open trough. Each turn of the flights traps a pocket of water and lifts it up the slope to discharge at the top. It handles large flows at low lift, passes debris and is self-regulating: flow follows the inlet level.

classification.configuration: Inclined open screw in a trough, 3 flights

introduction.summary: One of the oldest pumps: a large screw — helical flights welded around a central tube — is set at an angle in a close-fitting trough with its lower end in the inlet basin. As the screw turns slowly, each flight scoops water and carries it upward in a pocket bounded by the flights and the trough until it spills into the outlet channel. Flow adjusts itself to the inlet level, efficiency stays high over a wide range, and large solids and fish can pass, so screws are used for wastewater lift stations, storm water, land drainage and return sludge.

video_tutorials.title: Archimedes Screw Pump — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Archimedes Screw Pump.
An Archimedes screw pump is a large, slowly rotating screw set at an incline in an open trough.
Each turn of the flights traps a pocket of water and lifts it up the slope to discharge at the top.
It handles large flows at low lift, passes debris and is self-regulating: flow follows the inlet level.
Typical applications include wastewater treatment plant inlet lift; storm water and land drainage; return activated sludge; hydropower (reverse operation as a generator).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Screw (Central Tube + 3 Helical Flights).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Archimedes Screw Pump works.
Water at the lower basin fills the pockets between flights at the bottom of the screw.
The rotating screw lifts each pocket up the trough.
Pockets empty into the outlet channel at the top.
A gear reducer and motor drive the screw at low speed; bearings at both ends carry it.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Archimedes Screw Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Archimedes Screw Pump.
Check lower bearing lubrication.
Change gearbox oil.
Inspect flights and trough gap.
Watch for lower bearing failure: noise, wobble. Common cause: lubrication loss.
Watch for trough gap growth: lower flow. Common cause: wear of trough grout.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
